newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Primary market yawns.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Primary market yawns.

text.p: Few Brazilian names were expected to hit the Eurobond primary market this week, giving investors a little more time to absorb the huge supply of new paper issued over the past few weeks, traders said.

Gradiente could price its $100 million eight-year bond, with a five-year put, via CS First Boston sometime this week, traders said. The bond was seen coming at a spread of about 325 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
There was also talk that Parmalat's Brazil unit was putting together a $100 million eight-year bond, with puts and calls after three years. BankBoston was said to be the lead manager.
Bigger name corporates, like Petrobras and Eletrobras, and the republic were not expected to come to market with their deals until later in July, traders said.
"We're not going to see that much this week. The oversupply has caused widening in a lot of the new issues which still need to be absorbed," said one Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo.
IN SECONDARY TRADE, Brazilian Eurobonds ended last week mostly flat, after widening early in the week and tightening at the end.

Poor performers included CSN's 9.125 percent bond due 2007 ZYJJ, which closed last week at 305 bps after pricing the week before at 275. The bond was doing better early Monday, trading at a spread of 295 bps, market players said.
Traders said CSN was paying the price for its decision to double the bond from $300 million to $600 million, making it the largest debt issue from a private Brazilian corporation.

Also underperforming was Cesp's 9.125 percent 10-year bond ZYGZ, which closed last week at 304 bps over. The bond was in a virtual free-fall after pricing the week before at 280 over and tightening to the 260 bp level.
Oversupply of Brazilian 10-year paper was seen as a key reason for weakness in the CSN and Cesp issue, traders said.
Brazilian corporates and the republic over the past four weeks have issued more than $2.5 billion in new debt.
Top performers included Grupo Votorantim's eight-year putable bond ZYHB, which closed last week at a spread of 210 bps down from 220 bps, traders said.
